skill.name: environment-setup-guide
skill.description: Guides developers through platform-specific development environment setup, dependency installation, configuration files, and verification steps.
skill.summary: Create clear setup instructions for development tools, dependencies, environment variables, and verification checks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or covert data exfiltration was found in the Markdown skill. Most static hits are formatting or documentation false positives. Real risks remain in remote installers, sudo commands, Docker group membership, shell profile edits, and weak example credentials.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are downloaded and executed.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer official package manager steps, require source verification, and add checksum or signature checks before any shell execution.

remediation.issue: Several setup steps require sudo or privileged account changes.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation gates and explain the security impact before sudo commands or Docker group membership changes.

remediation.issue: The guide appends PATH changes to ~/.bashrc.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact shell profile diff first and tell users to back up or edit the file manually when possible.

remediation.issue: Example database credentials use weak placeholder values.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly non-secret placeholders and warn users to generate unique local passwords outside of source control.

remediation.issue: Environment file guidance could lead users to expose secrets.
remediation.suggestion: State that real .env values, API keys, npm tokens, and git credentials must not be pasted into AI chats or committed.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Installer Execution Without Integrity Verification
semantic_findings.description: The guide downloads installer scripts and then runs them with bash or sudo, but it does not require checksum or signature verification before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The linked lines show direct download followed by shell execution, including sudo for NodeSource and Docker. The guide asks for review in some cases but does not require cryptographic verification.

semantic_findings.title: Root-Equivalent Docker Group Enrollment
semantic_findings.description: The Docker setup adds the current user to the docker group without explaining that this can grant broad control over the host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exact command adds $USER to the docker group with sudo. Docker group access is widely treated as equivalent to elevated host control on many systems.

semantic_findings.title: Weak Example Database Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The Docker compose example uses a password-like value in the database URL and sets POSTGRES_PASSWORD to a weak literal example.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example contains a database URL with password@db and POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password. It is likely a local example, but it can normalize unsafe defaults if copied.

content.value_statement: New projects often fail because local tools, dependencies, and configuration steps are unclear. This skill creates structured setup guides with platform-specific commands, checks, and troubleshooting notes.
actual_capabilities: Lists required languages, package managers, databases, and development tools for a project.
Drafts macOS, Linux, and Windows setup steps using common package managers.
Explains how to create example environment files and document required variables.
Adds verification commands for installed tools, dependencies, services, and database connections.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for missing commands, permissions, ports, and service failures.
Outlines simple setup scripts for repeatable project onboarding.
limitations: It does not verify package integrity, checksums, or publisher signatures by itself.
It may suggest commands that require user review before execution.
It cannot know private project secrets unless users provide safe placeholder names.
It does not replace testing on each supported operating system.

use_cases.title: Create Project Onboarding Steps
use_cases.description: Turn project requirements into a clear setup guide for a new developer workstation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Machine
use_cases.description: Plan installation and verification steps when moving development work to a new computer.

use_cases.title: Document Environment Issues
use_cases.description: Add troubleshooting notes for common installation, PATH, port, and database connection problems.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Setup Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a development environment setup guide for my project. Ask for missing language, database, and operating system details before listing commands.

prompt_templates.title: Cross Platform Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for multiple operating systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write setup instructions for macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows. Include prerequisites, install steps, environment variables, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Onboarding Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these project requirements into an onboarding checklist. Include expected versions, configuration files, setup validation, and common fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Hardened Setup Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request focused on safer commands.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this setup guide for risky commands. Replace remote script execution where possible, add confirmation steps, and avoid exposing secrets.

output_examples.input: I need onboarding steps for a Node.js API with PostgreSQL.
output_examples.output: A guide with prerequisites, Node and database installation steps, environment variable placeholders, dependency installation, migration steps, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: My team has permission errors and port conflicts during setup.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting section that separates PATH issues, package permissions, running services, occupied ports, and database connection checks.

output_examples.input: Make our setup instructions safer before publishing them.
output_examples.output: A revised guide that avoids blind remote installer execution, warns before privileged commands, and replaces real secrets with placeholders.

best_practices: Use placeholder names for secrets, and never ask users to paste real secret values into chat.
Ask users to confirm before running commands that install software or change system settings.
Prefer official package manager instructions with version checks and rollback notes.
anti_patterns: Do not run downloaded installer scripts without review, checksums, or trusted source confirmation.
Do not append to shell startup files without showing the exact change first.
Do not commit .env files, tokens, passwords, or machine-specific paths to a repository.

faq.question: Can this skill run setup commands automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to produce guidance. Users should review and approve any command before execution.

faq.question: Does it support macOS, Linux, and Windows?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide includes examples for Homebrew, apt-style package managers, Chocolatey, winget, and direct installers.

faq.question: Can it document environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list required variables and placeholders, but users should not provide real secrets.

faq.question: Can it help with Docker setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft Docker and compose setup steps, including service checks and database connection tests.

faq.question: Does it validate that every command is safe?
faq.answer: No. Users should verify source trust, package signatures, permissions, and project-specific requirements.

faq.question: Is this useful for team onboarding?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn project requirements into repeatable onboarding steps with checks and troubleshooting notes.
